notes:
Evaluating Redwood as the inference backend for our VS Code Copilot extension (Nimbus Copilot). Primary engineering ask: stable streaming API with sub-100ms per-token emission on common dev machines and <30ms local editor latency budget when requests hit Redwood. Need model/version pinning at workspace or org level so customers can lock to vetted model hashes.

Key UX requirements (from product): inline suggestions that can be inserted with single keystroke, streaming partials for multi-line completions, graceful cancel and resume, and precise quota/rate limits per-seat mapped to SSO identity.

Security/compliance: corporate customers require SSO/SAML, SOC2 attestation, per-tenant audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and EU data residency for handful of customers. Also asked about on-prem fallback for air-gapped enterprise (longer term).

Engineering notes: tried demo streaming endpoints in hosted beta — saw spikes at ~180-250ms when model routing fallback occurred; want deterministic fallback behavior (e.g., fall back to quantized variant with wedge of latency increase rather than full error). Concern about token leakage in extension telemetry; asked about recommended client-side masking and server-side retention defaults.

Quote from CTO: "Need predictable serving more than raw model performance — developers notice jitter more than mean latency."

Target is low-latency interactive code completions (sub-100ms token latency on average), optional model pinning per workspace, and per-user quotas.
